item.query: https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2023/country-chapters/nigeria

item.text:
Buhari was Nigeria’s President and Commander-in-Chief throughout 2022, operating inside a federal system with real constitutional limits: the National Assembly, courts, federal-party rules, and, on military matters, Senate constraints and statutory oversight. The 2022 local prior already gives the structural baseline I would not re-fetch: persistent conflict/insecurity, rights repression, weak rule of law, corruption risk, and poor governance capacity. I used the web only for ruler-specific attribution, official statements, and narrative context.

**Retained sources**
1. [Past Heads of State and Presidents](https://statehouse.gov.ng/past-heads-of-state-and-presidents/) - The State House, undated roster page. Fact: lists Muhammadu Buhari as President from 29 May 2015 to 29 May 2023, so 2022 is squarely within his presidency. Period fit: exact office anchor. Ruler attribution: primary official roster. Limitations: no policy detail or event coverage. Contrary points: none on tenure.
2. [Nigeria 1999 (rev. 2023) Constitution](https://www.constituteproject.org/constitution/Nigeria_2023) - Constitute Project, 2023 revision of the constitution text. Fact: executive power is vested in the President; the President is Head of State and Commander-in-Chief; external combat deployment and war powers are constrained by the Senate/National Assembly; presidential term is four years and term limits apply. Period fit: stable legal framework governing 2022. Ruler attribution: legal authority/constraint source, not a performance source. Limitations: mirror text, not an official gazette scan. Contrary points: the constitution defines power but does not prove how fully Buhari exercised it.
3. [Independence Day Address By President Buhari On Nigeria’s 62nd Independence Anniversary Celebration](https://statehouse.gov.ng/independence-day-address-by-president-buhari-on-nigerias-62nd-indepedence-anniversary-celebration/) - The State House, 1 October 2022. Fact: Buhari speaks as sitting President, calls it his last Independence Day address, and foregrounds ASUU, education funding, health, floods, and climate stress. Period fit: direct 2022 self-report. Ruler attribution: strong for Buhari’s own priorities and framing. Limitations: self-justifying, no independent verification. Contrary points: claims about progress are not matched here against outside evidence.
4. [National Broadcast by President Buhari on Challenges of Currency Swap and State of the Nation](https://statehouse.gov.ng/national-broadcast-by-president-buhari-on-challenges-of-currency-swap-and-state-of-the-nation/) - The State House, 16 February 2023, but explicitly about the late-2022 currency swap rollout. Fact: Buhari says he authorized redesign of the N200/N500/N1000 notes in the last quarter of 2022, ties it to anti-corruption, money-in-circulation control, and election integrity, and acknowledges implementation hardship. Period fit: policy action rooted in late 2022, with follow-through in early 2023. Ruler attribution: excellent for direct policy intent. Limitations: official defense of a controversial policy. Contrary points: independent coverage shows shortages and disruption.
5. [Address By President Buhari At The 3rd Ministerial Performance Review Retreat](https://statehouse.gov.ng/address-by-president-buhari-at-the-3rd-ministerial-performance-review-retreat/) - The State House, 17 October 2022. Fact: Buhari says it is his last ministerial review retreat, frames the government as winding down, and presents the administration’s own account of delivery, infrastructure, security investment, social spending, and anti-corruption work. Period fit: very useful for end-of-term inherited-conditions and self-assessment framing. Ruler attribution: primary, but self-evaluative. Limitations: extensive achievement claims; not an external audit. Contrary points: the same period also saw major insecurity, labor unrest, and cash-policy turmoil.
6. [Loud blast, gunshots as suspected bandits attack Nigerian train](https://www.marketscreener.com/news/latest/Loud-blast-gunshots-as-suspected-bandits-attack-Nigerian-train-39894008/) - Reuters via MarketScreener, 29 March 2022. Fact: attack on the Abuja-Kaduna train killed at least seven, caused missing passengers, and underscored growing insecurity in Africa’s most populous country. Period fit: one of the year’s defining security shocks. Ruler attribution: external, independent event reporting. Limitations: Reuters reports the event, not the whole chain of responsibility. Contrary points: it documents the security failure, not a policy remedy.
7. [Suspected Islamist attack frees hundreds of prisoners in Nigeria](https://www.theguardian.com/world/2022/jul/06/suspected-boko-haram-attack-frees-hundreds-of-prisoners-in-nigeria-abuja) - The Guardian, 6 July 2022. Fact: the Kuje prison attack near Abuja freed nearly 900 inmates and became a symbol of security breakdown close to the capital. Period fit: major 2022 state-security stress test. Ruler attribution: independent reporting, useful for attributing consequences to Buhari’s security environment. Limitations: broad narrative piece; not a forensic investigation. Contrary points: the article reports the failure, not the administration’s internal response capacity.
8. [New Nigerian naira notes a rare sight on first day of circulation](https://www.marketscreener.com/news/latest/New-Nigerian-naira-notes-a-rare-sight-on-first-day-of-circulation-42566251/) - Reuters via MarketScreener, 16 December 2022. Fact: the new notes were scarce on day one, many Nigerians were still getting old notes, and Reuters notes the policy’s election sensitivity and cash-reliant economy impact. Period fit: best independent counterpoint to the official redesign narrative. Ruler attribution: external, independent; very useful for testing the presidency’s claims. Limitations: event reporting with partial market/economic framing. Contrary points: it directly undercuts the “smooth transition” story.
9. [Nigeria’s public university lecturers suspend strike after eight months](https://www.euronews.com/2022/10/15/nigeria-strike) - Reuters via Euronews, 15 October 2022. Fact: ASUU suspended an eight-month strike after presidential appeals; universities had been shut for most of the year. Period fit: major domestic governance and education event in 2022. Ruler attribution: strong for showing a direct presidential intervention, weak for deeper labor causation. Limitations: short news report, not a labor history. Contrary points: the suspension does not mean the underlying dispute was resolved cleanly.
10. [“Ina Mai Allah Wadai Da Kisan ‘Yan Arewa A Kudu” - Buhari](https://www.voahausa.com/a/ina-mai-allah-wadai-da-kisan-yan-arewa-a-kudu---buhari/6690725.html) - VOA Hausa, 7 August 2022. Fact: Buhari condemns killings of northerners living in southern Nigeria and promises investigation. Period fit: useful local-language confirmation of his public posture on intercommunal violence. Ruler attribution: strong, because it is ruler-specific and in Hausa. Limitations: brief report on a statement, not a broader investigation. Contrary points: the condemnation itself does not show effective protection or deterrence.
11. [World Report 2023: Nigeria](https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2023/country-chapters/nigeria) - Human Rights Watch, 2023 report page covering events of 2022. Fact: HRW says 2022 was marked by high insecurity, the Owo church killings, Kuje prison break, the Abuja-Kaduna train attack, abuses by security forces, and restrictions on expression/media. Period fit: very strong year-level synthesis. Ruler attribution: independent critical overview. Limitations: rights-focused, broad, and not a ruler-specific causal model. Contrary points: it highlights harms and abuses more than countervailing government gains.

**Compact event map**
- 29 March 2022: Abuja-Kaduna train attack exposes insecurity on a major transport corridor.
- 6 June 2022: Owo church massacre signals widening lethal violence beyond the northeast and northwest.
- 6 July 2022: Kuje prison attack humiliates the security apparatus near the capital; Buhari personally inspects the site.
- July to October 2022: ASUU strike drags on; Buhari pushes for a settlement and publicly frames the issue as a national education failure.
- 7 August 2022: Buhari condemns attacks on northerners in the south, showing ethnic/security tension.
- 1 October 2022: Independence Day address reveals his end-of-term framing, especially education, health, floods, and social welfare.
- 17 October 2022: performance retreat becomes an endgame self-audit and a signal that the administration is winding down.
- 23 November to December 2022: naira redesign and rollout become a major policy shock; Reuters coverage shows the scarcity and cash strain.
- February 2023 follow-through: Buhari defends the currency-swap policy as anti-corruption and election-integrity oriented.

**Chapter source plan**
- 1B: still weak in the local prior; use only if later work adds FAS/NTI/official defense or nuclear-capability material.
- 2B: train attack, Kuje, HRW security section, and the local UCDP/SIPRI prior already supplied.
- 3B: HRW, VOA Hausa, and the local CIRIGHTS/PTS/UCDP/V-Dem prior already supplied.
- 4B: Constitution plus Buhari’s 1 October and 17 October 2022 State House addresses.
- 5B: 17 October retreat plus the local GDP/population/WDI/Maddison prior already supplied.
- 6B: 1 October address plus the local WHO/HDI education-health prior already supplied.
- 7B: Constitution, 17 October retreat, and the local WGI/V-Dem corruption prior already supplied.
- 8B: Constitution, 17 October retreat, and the local WGI/governance-capacity prior already supplied.

If you want, I can turn this into a chapter-by-chapter evidence memo with only the reusable citations and no extra prose.
